message: 1 scheduled harvester(s) cannot run on this host: research/imagery_video.py requires ffmpeg, vision-ocr. Its manifest cannot grow from here, and every clip it would have screened was neither accepted nor rejected. The other 3 harvester(s) ran and their pools are committed.

research/imagery_video.py: ffmpeg: ffmpeg on PATH, to range-request one frame per probe time straight off the remote clip
vision-ocr: macOS with swiftc, to compile the Apple Vision OCR helper that reads the burned-in credit (gates B and C)

unblock: Decide where the Vision-dependent harvest runs: (a) give this workflow a `runs-on: macos-latest` job for the video harvester (ffmpeg, swiftc and Vision are on that image; 10x minute multiplier on a private repo), or (b) add `research/imagery_video.py --harvest` to the Mac's nightly batch (bin/batch-session.sh), which already commits and pushes repo state. Do NOT install a different OCR engine on Linux and do NOT accept clips unverified; loop/r2.py:verify_shorts records why both were rejected.
disposition_why: 'HARVESTER_TOOLING_ABSENT' is not in loop/stop_policy.json, so it is treated as needing a human. That is the default on purpose. issue #77 tracked this hold and has been CLOSED, but 'HARVESTER_TOOLING_ABSENT' is still holding on 2 item(s). A closed issue means handled; this is not handled.
